title: Sex and Laughter with Kyosai: Shunga from the Israel Goldman Collection

description.main: A new edition of Seigensha's bilingual survey of the erotic prints and paintings of Kawanabe Kyōsai (1831–1889), drawn from the Israel Goldman Collection in London, with texts by Ishigami Aki and Sadamura Koto.
description.extended:
A new edition of Seigensha's bilingual survey of the erotic prints and paintings of Kawanabe Kyōsai (1831–1889), drawn from the Israel Goldman Collection in London.

The authors, Ishigami Aki and Sadamura Koto, read the work through the period's own name for it. Shunga, "spring pictures," is a term that spread only in the Meiji era. In Kyōsai's lifetime such images were called warai-e, "pictures to laugh by." People of every class kept them, packed them into wedding trousseaus, and used them as talismans against fire and bad luck. Kyōsai's couples include aristocrats and monks, the old and the young, kami, demons and animals. The 228-page softcover is in Japanese and English. The first edition appeared in 2017.

Kyōsai trained in the Kano school and worked through Japan's change from shogunate to Meiji state. He called himself a "demon of painting" and drew caricature and satire throughout his career. In 1870 he was arrested over a picture that mocked the government. Israel Goldman, a London dealer in Japanese prints, paintings and illustrated books, holds one of the most complete collections of Kyōsai's work, which is also the source of Seigensha's Kyōsai's Animal Treasury.

notes: Works from the Israel Goldman Collection, London. Authors credited by the publisher: Ishigami Aki and Sadamura Koto. Japanese title 暁斎春画 ゴールドマン・コレクション 新装版. Release date 2026-04-22. Kawanabe Kyōsai has no official site.
